title: Reel: why your front pushes in flat turns
caption:
A front end that pushes wide in flat turns often has a fork riding too high in its travel. Too much compression and it never settles in, so there's less weight on the front tire.

Try a click out at a time and let it settle into the turn. If it still pushes, check sag: a rear that sits too low lifts the front too.

Tell Dialed Offroad the front pushes and it tells you which clicker and which way, one change at a time. Link in bio.

title: Reel: rear packing in chop? shock rebound
caption:
If the rear feels dead and harsh through braking bumps and chop, it may be packing down. Shock rebound is too slow, so it can't come back up before the next hit, and each bump starts lower in the stroke.

One click out opens the bleed gap a little and the rear comes back quicker. Go too far and it starts to kick instead. One click at a time, counted out from fully closed.

Tell Dialed Offroad the rear packs in chop and it tells you which way to go. Link in bio.

title: Reel: why the first laps feel harsh in the cold
caption:
Cold mornings make the fork feel harsh before you've touched a clicker. Cold oil is thicker, so it's harder to push through the piston and you get more damping than you set.

Give it a few laps before you judge anything. If it's still harsh once it's warm, then go a click out, one change at a time, counted out from fully closed.

Tell Dialed Offroad how it felt and it tells you which clicker and which way. Link in bio.
